blocker.summary: r480 (Piste A of the approved plan, the last of one explicitly authorized bounded attempt after r479) sent a single synthetic space-key confirm ~6s after a direct oracle-hybrid launch, reusing the exact xdotool keydown/keyup mechanism tools/ac6-oracle-run.py already implements (the engine run_gate.py loads dynamically). Result: still none of the three target shader draw states (r478: 09dd1c7cddae1141, 57b8e5f14b93cff4, 4dd456c4ea0923c1) were captured -- exactly the same 4 vertex shaders as r479's zero-input attempt. Notable new finding: this direct launch's boot took over 700 real seconds (CPU continuously active, not frozen) before being manually stopped -- an order of magnitude beyond any normal run_gate.py route duration, confirming (without explaining) a real boot-pacing divergence between the oracle-hybrid and native products noted by r479. A clean shutdown via `xdotool windowclose` worked (process exited in ~20s), but produced NO persistent .xpso/.xsh cache file despite that -- only the same .ucode shader dump as before. Explicit recommendation: pause Piste A here -- 5 consecutive cycles (r476-r480) of diminishing returns on this specific sub-problem, each attempt more granular than the last, without reaching the target content. Named for r481: Piste A paused pending user confirmation; Piste B (commit the stabilized native backlog, r433-r479) and Piste C (HUD guard-rail) from the approved plan remain open, independent, and ready to start without depending on Piste A's resolution.
